cards.what: Every campaign has three parts: the market you reach, the message you send, and the media that carries it. Pick the market first, and none of the three works alone.
cards.remix: Name one buyer before you write a word, then post where they already scroll, not where you do. Your For You page is not market research.

cards.idea: Always an offer. Always a reason.
cards.what: Two of the book's ten rules: every piece of marketing makes an offer, and every piece gives a reason to respond right now, not someday.
cards.remix: Every post ends with one ask. Every offer gets one real deadline or limit: a drop date, a batch size, or a bonus that really expires. Resetting timers? Sus.

cards.what: Follow-up is one of the book's ten rules. Anyone who didn't answer the first time hears from you again, on purpose, instead of being forgotten.
cards.remix: Three messages, not one: a reminder, a last call, then a new angle. Send them by DM, email, or text (with consent). One post is not a launch.

cards.what: Stop chasing prospects. Draw the right ones to you, then run three systems: one that attracts, one that converts, and one that keeps customers coming back.
cards.remix: Content attracts, DMs and a landing page convert, a newsletter retains. Cold-DMing strangers is door-to-door sales with worse Wi-Fi.

cards.what: Answer the buyer's real question: why you over every other option, including a competitor, doing it themselves, or doing nothing? Domino's "30 minutes or less, guaranteed" is the model.
cards.remix: Your "why you" has to fit in a bio line and a 3-second hook. If it takes a paragraph, it's a podcast episode, not a reason.

cards.what: One of the 28 steps in the book's sales-letter system: make a damaging admission. Name your flaw openly instead of hiding it.
cards.remix: Say the flaw first: "It's not cheap. Here's why." Or: "Ships in 3 weeks, because I make each one by hand." Honesty reads as real. Filters don't.

cards.book: No B.S. Guide to Direct Response Social Media Marketing
cards.what: Social media counts only when it produces measurable sales: right market, right message, right media, and results measured in money. Likes, views, viral moments: none of it goes in the bank.
cards.remix: Score every platform by sales per hour you spend there, not by followers. Sales are the scoreboard. Aura farming is a hobby, not a business model.

cards.book: No B.S. Guide to Maximum Referrals and Customer Retention
cards.what: Customers stay when three things add up: shared interest (you connect beyond the product), shared space (you keep showing up in their life), and shared concern (you care about their results).
cards.remix: Interest: behind-the-scenes posts. Space: a Close Friends list, Discord, or a surprise mailer. Concern: DM buyers a week later asking how it's going.

cards.what: Question every belief you hold about price. The book counts having no premium option as a pricing failure, and says discount only for a specific reason that gets you something back.
cards.remix: Before you cut the price, add a tier above it. Discount only for prepay or a bundle. A forever code? Discount Goblin behavior. Buyers learn to wait.

cards.what: Being a little hard to get draws buyers in. It only works with the right positioning and enough interest that you actually turn some people away.
cards.remix: Run a waitlist or an application instead of an open door. Cap it at what you can actually deliver: can coach 5 people? Say 5, and mean it.

cards.what: Buyers in a good mood buy more, so humor is a persuasion tool, not a distraction.
cards.remix: My excuse for the jokes. Open with the laugh, close with the offer. A funny post with no ask is a free stand-up set.

Kennedy's order in No B.S. Direct Marketing: market first (one specific buyer), then message, then media. My take: your months of work are proof. They go after the buyer's problem, never before it.
